title: Crispy Calamari Rings
ingredients: 14 oz fresh or thawed calamari rings
3.5 oz durum wheat semolina flour (or corn flour)
description: No oil splatters in the kitchen or lingering fried smell in the house. The semolina-crusted calamari rings get crispy in 8 minutes and remain tender inside.
instructions: Pat the calamari rings perfectly dry with paper towels: this is the most important step.
Place the calamari rings and semolina flour in a plastic bag, seal it, and shake well to coat them evenly.
Remove the calamari, shaking off any excess flour, and arrange them in a single layer in the air fryer basket.
Spray plenty of olive oil over all the calamari (there should be no dry white flour spots).
Cook at 390°F for 8-10 minutes, shaking the basket halfway through cooking.
tip: Remilled semolina flour is essential to replicate the rustic and crispy effect of authentic Italian fried seafood.

title: Classic Italian Breaded Cutlet
description: The quintessential Italian cutlet, a favorite among children. Air-fried, it's light and easy to digest, yet boasts a crispy crust indistinguishable from one fried in a pan.
instructions: Lightly pound the meat if it's too thick.
Dip the cutlets first in the beaten egg (with a pinch of salt) and then in the breadcrumbs, pressing firmly with your palms.
Preheat the air fryer to 375°F.
Generously spray the bottom of the air fryer basket and the surface of the cutlet with cooking spray.
Cook for 12-15 minutes. Flip the cutlet halfway through cooking and spray the other side with oil.
tip: Add one tablespoon of Parmesan cheese and half a minced garlic clove to the breadcrumbs for an even more flavorful coating.

title: Stuffed Meatloaf
ingredients: 1.1 lbs mixed ground meat (beef and pork)
1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese and 1/2 cup breadcrumbs
Extra virgin olive oil and rosemary
description: The king of Sunday dinners. Cooked whole in the air fryer basket, it forms a delicious crispy crust while sealing in the gooey cheese and meat juices.
instructions: Mix the ground meat with the egg, Parmesan cheese, breadcrumbs, salt, and pepper until you get a firm mixture.
Spread the mixture on a sheet of parchment paper, forming a rectangle about 1/2 inch thick.
Stuff with the ham slices and cheese, leaving the edges free.
Roll up the meatloaf using the parchment paper and seal the ends well.
Brush the surface with olive oil and rosemary. Place in the air fryer basket (keeping a perforated sheet of parchment paper underneath) and cook at 355°F for 35-40 minutes.
tip: Let the meatloaf cool for 10 minutes outside the air fryer before slicing, otherwise the slices will break apart.

title: Air Fryer Sausage and Potatoes
ingredients: 1 whole garlic clove and fresh rosemary sprigs
description: A beloved one-pan dinner in Italy. Cooked together, the savory sausage fat drips onto the potatoes, making them crispy on the outside and incredibly tender on the inside.
instructions: Cut potatoes into medium cubes (about 1 inch / 2-3 cm) and soak them in cold water for 10 minutes. Dry them thoroughly.
Cut sausage into large chunks.
In a bowl, mix potatoes, sausage, garlic, rosemary, olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Pour everything into the air fryer basket and cook at 385°F for 20-25 minutes.
Vigorously shake the air fryer basket every 7-8 minutes to ensure even browning of the meat and vegetables.
tip: If the potatoes are cut too large, they might remain raw. Try to maintain a uniform cube size.

title: Abruzzese Lamb Skewers
description: The inimitable street food from Abruzzo. The extreme heat renders the fat from the lamb cubes, making them succulent and slightly charred, just like on the traditional charcoal grill.
instructions: If the skewers are too long for your air fryer basket, break off the wooden tips or cut them with scissors.
Arrange the arrosticini in the basket, avoiding stacking them too high (maximum two crossed layers).
Cook at 400°F for 8-10 minutes.
Flip the skewers halfway through cooking.
Remove the very hot arrosticini, place them in aluminum foil, salt generously, and close the packet for one minute before serving.
tip: The salt must be added strictly raw and only AFTER cooking, otherwise the meat will lose its juices and become tough and dry.

title: Air-Fried Artichokes (Giudia Style)
ingredients: Fine sea salt and black pepper
description: A homemade and lighter interpretation of the famous Roman-Jewish dish. The outer leaves open up like a flower, becoming crispy like potato chips, while the heart remains tender.
instructions: Clean the artichokes by removing the toughest outer leaves. Trim off the fibrous part of the stem.
Gently tap the artichokes upside down on a cutting board to help the petals open up into a flower shape.
Generously mix with olive oil, salt, and pepper, making sure the seasoning gets between the leaves.
Place them upside down in the air fryer basket and cook at 355°F for 10 minutes.
Flip them right side up and cook for the final 5 minutes at 400°F to crisp up the open petals.
tip: After cleaning, soak them in lemon water to prevent them from browning before cooking.

title: Stuffed Tomatoes and Bell Peppers
ingredients: 2 large cluster tomatoes and 2 medium bell peppers
approx. 2/3 cup uncooked Arborio rice (or ground meat)
Extra virgin olive oil, salt, fresh basil
description: A classic summer dish from Italian grandmothers. Hollowed out and stuffed with rice or ground meat, the vegetables soften, releasing their sweet juices directly into the flavorful filling.
instructions: Slice off the tops of the vegetables, scoop out the seeds, and, for the tomatoes, blend the scooped-out inner pulp.
Season the uncooked rice (or ground meat) with the tomato pulp, olive oil, salt, Parmesan cheese, and basil.
Fill the hollowed vegetables 3/4 full (the rice will expand during cooking). Cover with their respective tops or with a sprinkle of breadcrumbs.
Gently place them in the air fryer basket.
Cook at 355°F for 20-25 minutes, or until the vegetables are tender and the filling is perfectly cooked.
tip: If using uncooked rice, ensure the filling is very moist and watery (add the tomato pulp) so the grains cook thoroughly inside.

title: Rosemary Diced Potatoes
description: Not your typical French fries, but true Italian 'baked' potatoes, diced and flavored with garlic and rosemary. Extra crispy on the edges.
instructions: Peel the potatoes and cut them into 3/4-1 inch cubes. Rinse them thoroughly to remove starch and meticulously pat them dry with a clean kitchen towel.
In a bowl, season them with olive oil, the crushed garlic cloves (skin on), and rosemary needles.
Pour them evenly into the air fryer basket.
Cook at 385°F for 20 minutes.
Pull out the drawer every 6-7 minutes to shake the potatoes vigorously; this will create that crispy outer crust. Salt only at the end.
tip: Keeping the garlic cloves unpeeled (skin on) releases aroma without burning and becoming bitter under the air fryer's powerful fan.

title: Savory Ricotta and Spinach Tart
ingredients: 1 round sheet of puff pastry or shortcrust pastry
10.5 oz (about 2 cups) cooked, sautéed, and squeezed spinach
description: The ultimate weeknight savior, the savory tart! It keeps a crispy and dry base and a rich, creamy filling, cooking in half the time of a conventional oven.
instructions: Squeeze the cooked spinach very well and chop it. Mix it in a bowl with the ricotta, egg, Parmesan, salt, and nutmeg.
Unroll the pastry sheet, leaving it on its parchment paper, and place it in a round baking dish suitable for your air fryer basket.
Prick the bottom with a fork and pour in the filling, leveling it out.
Fold the edges of the pastry inwards.
Cook at 340°F for 20-25 minutes. If the edges brown too quickly, cover them with a bit of aluminum foil during the last 5 minutes.
tip: Place the baking dish directly on the perforated rack of the air fryer basket: the air circulation from the bottom will ensure the pastry base cooks without becoming soggy.

title: Roasted Chestnuts
description: The classic Italian autumn treat. The air fryer makes them perfect: crispy on the outside, tender on the inside, and incredibly easy to peel thanks to the preliminary soaking.
instructions: Make a horizontal cut on the 'belly' of each chestnut using a sharp knife.
Immerse the chestnuts in a bowl of warm water for at least 15 minutes. This trick softens the peel.
Drain and dry them very well with a kitchen towel.
Place them in the air fryer basket without overcrowding and cook at 390°F for 15-20 minutes (depending on their size).
Remove them from the air fryer and wrap them in a damp cloth for 5 minutes: they will peel instantly!
tip: Don't skip the soaking and the resting in the damp cloth: these are the secrets to prevent them from drying out too much.

title: Light Arancini and Supplì
description: The masterpiece of Sicilian and Roman street food. With the vortex of hot air, the mozzarella heart melts perfectly, while the breadcrumb shell becomes a spectacle of crispiness.
instructions: Ensure the arancini or supplì are cold from the fridge before cooking them; this will help them maintain their shape.
Spray the breaded surface generously with cooking spray; this is essential for browning the breadcrumbs without drying them out.
Place them in the air fryer basket, spaced apart.
Cook at 390°F for 15-18 minutes.
Gently turn the pieces halfway through cooking and give them another light spray of oil if you see any white breadcrumb areas.
tip: If you prepare them at home, use a 'binding mixture' (water and flour) before the breadcrumbs to make them impenetrable and extra crispy.

title: Potato Croquettes (Panzarotti)
ingredients: 1.1 lbs (about 2 cups) cold mashed potatoes (floury potatoes recommended)
about 1/2 cup (1.8 oz) grated Parmesan cheese
Mozzarella cheese, cut into small strips or cubes for stuffing
description: Classic Neapolitan potato croquettes, also known as panzarotti. Soft on the inside and golden on the outside, they won't open or fall apart thanks to the gentle air frying.
instructions: Combine the cold, dry mashed potatoes with the egg, Parmesan cheese, salt, pepper, and parsley. Mix well until everything is incorporated.
Shape the mixture into cylinders, inserting a piece of well-drained mozzarella in the center of each one.
Dip the croquettes first in beaten egg, then roll them thoroughly in breadcrumbs to coat.
Refrigerate for 15 minutes to allow them to firm up, which helps prevent them from breaking during cooking.

Arrange the croquettes in the air fryer basket in a single layer, making sure not to overcrowd. Spray them lightly with cooking spray and cook at 400°F for 12-14 minutes, flipping them halfway through to ensure even browning.
tip: The secret to preventing them from bursting is to use yellow-fleshed, older, or floury potatoes that are low in water content.

title: Quick Olive Oil Focaccia (Schiacciatina Flatbread)
ingredients: About 9 oz (approx. 1/2 lb) pizza dough (store-bought or homemade, risen)
description: Perfect for serving with cured meats and cheeses. A thin focaccia, perfectly oiled, crispy on the bottom, and topped with coarse salt and rosemary.
instructions: Cut a circle of parchment paper the size of your air fryer basket and grease it with a drizzle of olive oil.
Spread the dough on the parchment paper, using your fingertips to create the classic dimples.
In a small cup, whisk together 2 tablespoons of olive oil and 1 tablespoon of water to form an emulsion (brine).
Spread this emulsion over the focaccia, then sprinkle with coarse salt and rosemary.
Bake at 375°F for 12-15 minutes, or until the surface is golden brown and crispy.
tip: The water and oil brine is the bakers' secret trick: it prevents the focaccia from drying out too much with the circulating air and keeps it soft inside.

title: Nutella/Jam Stuffed Puff Pastry Cornetti
ingredients: Nutella, pistachio cream, or jam of choice
1 egg yolk or a dash of milk for brushing
description: Sunday breakfast ready in a mere 10 minutes. Simple puff pastry transforms into fragrant, puffy, and utterly delicious mini croissants.
instructions: Unroll the circular puff pastry and cut it into wedges (like pizza slices), forming 8 triangles.
Place a teaspoon of your favorite filling at the wide base of each triangle.
Roll the pastry from the base towards the tip, then gently curve the ends to form the croissant shape.
Arrange them spaced apart in the air fryer basket on parchment paper and brush the surface with a dash of milk.
Cook at 340°F for 10-12 minutes until golden brown and puffed. Dust with powdered sugar once cooled.
tip: Don't overfill: the quick heat will make the filling fluid and it might leak out, tearing the pastry.
