title: Eggplant Parmesan
ingredients: Extra virgin olive oil, as needed
description: The quintessential Italian classic, in a lighter version that's incredibly gooey and flavorful.
instructions: Slice the eggplant into thin slices, about 1/4 inch thick.
Brush the slices with a very small amount of oil and pre-cook them in the air fryer basket for 8 minutes at 355°F.
Take a small baking dish suitable for your air fryer and assemble the layers: sauce, eggplant, cubed mozzarella, Parmesan, and basil.
Bake the little Parmigiana at 355°F for 12 minutes, until the surface forms a golden crust.
tip: Use block mozzarella (the kind for pizza) instead of fresh mozzarella: it will release less liquid, and the Parmigiana won't be watery.

title: Grandma's Meatballs with Sauce
ingredients: 10.6 oz mixed ground meat (beef and pork)
1 slice stale bread, soaked in milk
Salt and black pepper, to taste
description: Soft, succulent, and perfect for 'scarpetta' (mopping up the sauce). Authentic Italian meatballs, quickly cooked in an air fryer.
instructions: Squeeze out the stale bread and mix it in a bowl with the ground meat, egg, Parmesan cheese, parsley, salt, and pepper.
Form walnut-sized round meatballs.
Cook the meatballs alone in the air fryer basket at 375°F for 10 minutes to seal them and make them crispy on the outside.
Transfer them to an oven-safe dish, cover with warm tomato sauce, and let them infuse with flavor in the air fryer for another 5 minutes.
tip: Sealing the meatballs without sauce first allows the meat to retain all its juices inside, keeping them extremely tender.

title: Sicilian Ragù Arancini
ingredients: 1.5 cups of leftover, cold risotto rice
1.8 oz of diced Caciocavallo or Provolone cheese
description: The iconic Sicilian street food, super crispy on the outside with a gooey, cheesy center, without the grease of deep-frying.
instructions: Mix the cold rice with saffron dissolved in one tablespoon of hot water.
Take a handful of rice, flatten it in your palm, and place a spoonful of ragù, peas, and a cube of cheese in the center.
Close the rice around the filling, forming a ball (or a cone), then dip it in a light batter of water and flour, and finally coat generously in breadcrumbs.
Spray the arancini with olive oil on all sides and cook at 400°F for 15 minutes, flipping halfway through.
tip: The rice must be cold from the fridge! If you use freshly made or lukewarm rice, the arancini will fall apart.

title: Ascolana-Style Olives
description: A classic appetizer from the Marche region. Savory meat stuffing encased in a breaded green olive.
instructions: Arrange the olives in a single layer in the air fryer basket, spaced apart.
Lightly and evenly spray the olives with cooking oil to ensure a golden crust.
Cook at 400°F for 10 minutes, shaking the basket halfway through to brown them evenly on all sides.
tip: If using frozen olives, do not thaw them! Place them directly from the freezer, adding 2-3 extra minutes to the timer.

title: Ligurian Stuffed Zucchini
description: Zucchini boats with a rich and flavorful filling, perfectly gratinéed in just a few minutes.
instructions: Cut the zucchini in half, scoop out the pulp with a spoon, and finely chop the pulp.
In a bowl, combine the chopped zucchini pulp, ground meat, egg, Parmesan cheese, salt, pepper, and marjoram.
Fill the zucchini boats with the mixture and sprinkle the surface with breadcrumbs and a drizzle of olive oil.
Cook in the air fryer basket at 355°F for 18 minutes, until a beautiful golden crust forms.
tip: For softer zucchini, blanch the empty zucchini boats in salted water for 3 minutes before filling them.

title: Roman Supplì 'Al Telefono'
ingredients: About 1.5 cups (8.8 oz) cooked rice with tomato sauce or ragù (well chilled)
3.5 oz fresh mozzarella, cut into strips
description: Rome's pride: tomato rice croquettes that stretch 'like a telephone cord' when broken in half.
instructions: Take two tablespoons of cold rice, flatten them in your palm, and place two or three strips of mozzarella in the center.
Close them, shaping them into the classic oval and elongated supplì form.
Dip the supplì in the beaten egg, then roll them in breadcrumbs, ensuring they are well coated.
Spray with olive oil and cook at 400°F for 12 minutes, flipping halfway through.
tip: The mozzarella must be very dry; otherwise, during cooking, it will wet the rice and cause the supplì to open up.

title: Mozzarella in Carrozza
ingredients: 4 slices of sandwich bread or Pullman loaf
description: The Neapolitan comfort food: fried sandwiches with a warm, super-stretchy heart, in a non-greasy version.
instructions: Remove the crusts from the bread and place a thick slice of mozzarella between two slices of bread, pressing the edges firmly.
Quickly dip the edges of the sandwich in a little milk, then dredge the entire sandwich in the beaten egg, and finally in the breadcrumbs.
Spray generously with cooking oil spray on both sides.
Cook at 375°F for 10 minutes, flipping the sandwich halfway through for even browning.
tip: If you like a stronger flavor, add an anchovy or a slice of cooked ham along with the mozzarella.

title: Crispy Fried Calamari
ingredients: 14 oz fresh or thawed squid rings
description: The classic Italian mixed fried seafood, but incredibly light and without messy oil splatters in the kitchen.
instructions: Thoroughly pat dry the squid rings with paper towels. They must be completely free of water.
Place them in a plastic bag with a generous amount of semolina flour and shake well to coat.
Arrange them in the air fryer basket in a single layer without overlapping (cook in two batches if necessary) and spray with olive oil spray.
Cook at 400°F for 10-12 minutes. Salt only at the end and serve with lemon.
tip: The secret to non-rubbery calamari is perfect drying and the use of semolina flour, which provides much more 'crunch' than all-purpose flour.

title: Stuffed Bell Peppers with Meat
ingredients: 1 slice of bread, soaked and squeezed
Parsley, garlic powder, salt, and pepper
description: A hearty, flavorful, and rustic main course or side dish typical of Italian Sundays.
instructions: Cut the bell peppers in half lengthwise and remove the seeds and white membranes.
Mix the meat with the squeezed bread, egg, parsley, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Fill the pepper halves with the mixture, sprinkle with cheese, and add a drizzle of olive oil.
Cook in the air fryer basket at 356°F for 25 minutes until the peppers are tender and the meat is thoroughly cooked.
tip: To prevent the top from burning before the peppers are cooked, cover them with a small piece of aluminum foil for the first 15 minutes.

title: Rustic Sausage and Potatoes
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
description: The perfect duo of Italian home cooking. The sausage cooks and gently flavors the potatoes.
instructions: Peel the potatoes and cut them into regular chunks of about 1 inch. Season them with oil, salt, pepper, rosemary, and the peeled garlic.
Cut the sausages into large pieces (or leave them whole, pricking the skin).
Place everything together in the air fryer basket.
Cook at 375°F for about 22 minutes, shaking the basket well every 7-8 minutes to let the flavors meld.
tip: Do not use too much oil on the potatoes: the fat naturally released by the sausage during cooking will make them glossy and flavorful.

title: Pasta Omelette (Frittata di Maccheroni)
ingredients: Salt and plenty of black pepper
Extra virgin olive oil to taste
description: The famous Neapolitan pasta omelette: a perfect crispy crust on the outside, soft on the inside. The perfect food for picnics.
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk the eggs with the Parmesan, salt, pepper, and diced cured meat.
Add the pasta (it does not matter if it was already dressed with sauce or plain) and mix well.
Pour the mixture into a parchment paper-lined pan suitable for your air fryer.
Cook at 355°F for 18 minutes. Use a toothpick to verify that the egg in the center is fully set.
tip: The more pepper you add, the more authentic it will be! If your pan is deep, it might take a few extra minutes of cooking time.

title: Milanese Breaded Cutlet
ingredients: 2 pork loin or veal slices (pounded thin)
description: The timeless breaded cutlet: thick or thin, this is the main course loved by both adults and children.
instructions: Pound the meat lightly if necessary. Dip each slice first into the beaten egg and then into the breadcrumbs, pressing firmly to coat.
Preheat the air fryer to 375°F for 3 minutes.
Place the cutlets in the basket and spray the entire surface evenly with olive oil spray.
Cook for 7 minutes, then flip, spray the other side, and cook for another 7 minutes. Salt only before serving.
tip: Add a pinch of chopped parsley and Parmesan cheese to the breadcrumbs for an even tastier coating.

title: Crispy Roman-Style Artichokes
ingredients: Extra virgin olive oil to taste
description: A quick and healthy take on the classic Roman Jewish-style artichokes. Crispy, chip-like leaves with a tender heart.
instructions: Clean the artichokes by removing the tough outer leaves and trimming the tips. Soak them in water with lemon juice.
Dry them thoroughly and 'bang' them upside down on a cutting board to make them open up like a flower.
Season by inserting a minced mixture of garlic, parsley, calamint, salt, pepper, and a generous drizzle of olive oil into the center.
Place them upside down in the air fryer basket and cook at 355°F for 15 minutes, until the outer leaves are toasted and crispy.
tip: The secret is drying them well: if there is water trapped between the leaves, the artichoke will steam instead of fry.

title: Air Fryer Stuffed Zucchini Blossoms
ingredients: All-purpose flour and breadcrumbs as needed
description: An irresistible appetizer. Melty filling and crispy breading, perfect for summer.
instructions: Gently clean the blossoms by removing the internal pistil without breaking them.
Place a small piece of (well-dried) mozzarella and an anchovy into each blossom, then twist the tip to close it.
Instead of a classic liquid batter, dip them in beaten egg and then in breadcrumbs (this allows for air frying).
Spray generously with cooking spray and cook at 375°F for 8 minutes.
tip: Air fryers do not handle liquid batters well (they drip through). The breadcrumb coating is the secret to a top-tier result.

title: Tomato and Basil Bruschetta
description: The world's most famous Italian appetizer. Air-toasted bread becomes golden and fragrant in just a few minutes.
instructions: Dice the tomatoes into very small cubes and season them in a bowl with olive oil, salt, and hand-torn basil. Let rest.
Place the plain bread slices in the air fryer at 400°F for 4-5 minutes to toast them.
Remove the bread and lightly rub a raw garlic clove over the warm surface.
Distribute the tomato mixture over the slices and serve immediately.
tip: Always toast the bread on its own! If you add the tomatoes before cooking, the tomato juice will ruin the crunchiness of the bread.

title: Air Fryer Gnocchi Appetizer Bites
description: Not the traditional Emilian 'Gnocco Fritto', but real potato gnocchi turned crispy like potato chips. Highly addictive!
instructions: In a bowl, toss the RAW gnocchi straight from the package with the olive oil, salt, paprika, and rosemary.
Pour them into the air fryer basket in a single layer.
Cook at 400°F for 10-12 minutes, shaking the basket well halfway through.
Serve hot as an appetizer, perfect for dipping in cheese fondue or marinara sauce.
tip: Make sure to use fresh (soft) gnocchi, not the shelf-stable dry ones, for the best results.

title: Ricotta Castagnole (Carnival Fritters)
ingredients: Grated zest of 1 lemon or orange
Cooking spray oil and milk as needed
description: Classic Italian Carnival treats: soft, citrus-scented dough balls, air-fried guilt-free.
instructions: In a bowl, mix the ricotta with the egg, sugar, and citrus zest.
Add the flour and baking powder, kneading until you have a smooth dough (if it's too stiff, add 1 tablespoon of milk).
Form small balls slightly larger than a walnut and lightly spray them with oil.
Air fry at 355°F for 10 minutes. Immediately after removing them (while still very hot), roll them in granulated sugar to coat.
tip: Lightly spraying with oil before cooking is the magic trick to help the sugar stick once they are baked.

title: Quick Apulian Panzerotti
ingredients: Extra virgin olive oil for brushing
description: Half-moon pockets filled with tomato and mozzarella. The Apulian street food classic ready in 8 minutes.
instructions: Unroll the pizza dough and cut out circles using a large cup or a cookie cutter.
Place a teaspoon of tomato puree seasoned with salt and oregano, and a little mozzarella in the center of each circle.
Fold into a half-moon shape and seal the edges perfectly by pressing them with the tines of a fork.
Brush the surface with a thin layer of oil and cook at 400°F for 8 minutes, until the dough is golden and puffed.
tip: Seal the edges like your life depends on it! If they open during cooking, the cheese will burn on the bottom of the air fryer.

title: Soft Rosemary Focaccia
ingredients: 0.18 oz fresh yeast (or 0.07 oz active dry yeast)
Fresh rosemary and coarse salt for topping
description: Tall, fluffy, and featuring the classic dimples on top. Air-fried to perfection, it stays fragrant and is ideal for sandwiches.
instructions: Dissolve the yeast in the lukewarm water, then add the flour, oil, and finally the salt. Knead until you have an elastic dough.
Let the dough rise, covered, for 2 hours or until it has doubled in volume.
Spread the dough into a round baking pan (sized for your air fryer basket) greased with oil. Make the classic 'dimples' with your fingertips.
Top with an emulsion of water and oil (in equal parts), coarse salt, and rosemary. Bake at 340°F for 18 minutes.
tip: Do not use temperatures higher than 340°F for large leavened goods in an air fryer, or they will burn on the outside while remaining raw on the inside.

title: Air Fryer Calamari and Shrimp
keywords: fried, crispy, delicious, seafood, main course, calamari, shrimp, air fryer
ingredients: 7 oz fresh or thawed calamari rings
Durum wheat semolina flour as needed
description: The classic seafood fry everyone loves. Air-fried for a dry, crispy, and easily digestible result.
instructions: Thoroughly pat the calamari and shrimp dry with paper towels. This is the most important step!
Place the seafood in a plastic bag with plenty of semolina flour and shake well to coat evenly.
Sift off the excess flour using a strainer and arrange the seafood in the air fryer basket in a single layer without overlapping.
Spray generously with cooking oil on all sides.
Cook at 400°F for 12 minutes, shaking the basket halfway through and giving it another spritz of oil if you see white flour spots.
tip: Do not use all-purpose flour! Durum wheat semolina flour is the real secret to achieving a crispy crust in the air fryer.

title: Air Fryer Mixed Fried Fish (Frittura di Paranza)
keywords: fried, crispy, delicious, fish, seafood, main course, paranza, small fish, anchovies
ingredients: 14 oz mixed small fish (anchovies, red mullet, whiting, silversides)
Durum wheat semolina flour, as needed
Extra virgin olive oil or vegetable oil spray
description: Authentic fisherman-style fried fish. Small, flavorful fish meant to be eaten whole, as crispy as potato chips.
instructions: Rinse the small fish quickly and gut the slightly larger ones (silversides can be left whole). Pat them very dry.
Dredge them thoroughly in the semolina flour and shake off the excess.
Place them in the preheated air fryer basket. Do not overcrowd them!
Lightly spray the surface of the fish evenly with oil.
Cook at 400°F for 10 minutes. Gently turn the fish with tongs halfway through cooking. Salt only after cooking.
tip: Mixed small fish are delicate: do not shake the basket violently halfway through; use silicone tongs to turn them.

title: Air Fryer Crispy Baby Squid
keywords: frying, fried, crispy, delicious, seafood, fish, main dish, baby squid, calamari
ingredients: Durum wheat semolina flour, to taste
description: Baby squid are packed with flavor. They fry whole in just a few minutes and stay incredibly tender on the inside.
instructions: Make sure the baby squid are well cleaned, but leave them whole (the tentacles will become the crispiest part). Pat them dry with paper towels.
Dredge them in the durum wheat semolina, shaking off any excess to avoid a pasty texture.
Arrange them in the air fryer basket in a single layer and spray them evenly with cooking oil.
Cook at 400°F for just 8-10 minutes maximum. Remove them as soon as the small tentacles are golden and curled.
Season generously with salt and serve immediately.
tip: Watch the time carefully: baby squid cook in a flash. Exceeding 10 minutes will make them rubbery and bitter.

title: Golden Crispy Shrimp
keywords: air fry, fried, crispy, delicious, seafood, main course, shrimp, prawns
ingredients: 10.6 oz shrimp tails (or prawns), peeled with tails left on
Semolina or fine cornmeal flour, to taste
description: A shrimp-only fry that is sweet and juicy on the inside, wrapped in a golden breading. Perfect as a chic appetizer.
instructions: Clean the shrimp by removing the shell and the digestive tract (the black vein on the back), leaving the tail intact for a better presentation and easy handling.
Pat them dry thoroughly. On a plate, mix the semolina flour with a pinch of salt and the paprika.
Dredge the shrimp in the flour, pressing lightly to ensure it adheres well.
Place them in the air fryer basket and spray generously with oil on both sides.
Cook at 400°F for about 8-10 minutes, flipping halfway through, until they have a vibrant color and a golden crust.
tip: Adding a little sweet paprika to the flour not only adds flavor but also helps give the shrimp that beautiful golden-red color typical of restaurant-style fried food.

title: Rustic Skin-on Fries
description: All the authentic taste of rustic potatoes, with the skin adding flavor and texture. Ready in a flash and perfectly golden brown thanks to air circulation.
instructions: Place the frozen fries in the basket, trying to distribute them in an even layer.
Do not add extra oil, as the product is already pre-oiled.
Set the cooking temperature to 400°F for 18-20 minutes.
Shake the basket vigorously halfway through cooking to ensure they become crispy all over.
tip: Arrange them in a single layer if possible for maximum crispiness.
keywords: frying, fried, crispy, tasty, potatoes, frozen, vegetables, side dish, vegetarian, vegan, fast, easy, quick

title: Homemade Corn Tortilla Chips
ingredients: Salsa (e.g., guacamole or Mexican) for serving
description: Turn simple tortillas into crispy chips, ideal for happy hour. Much healthier than store-bought versions, they are perfect for dipping in guacamole.
instructions: Cut each tortilla in half, then divide each half into quarters to obtain 8 triangular wedges per tortilla.
In a bowl, toss the tortilla triangles with olive oil and salt, making sure they are well coated.
Preheat the air fryer to 300°F.
Arrange the tortillas in the basket and cook for 8 minutes.
Shake the basket halfway through cooking to ensure crispiness on both sides. Serve hot or at room temperature.
tip: Make sure not to overlap them too much in the basket; if necessary, cook in two separate batches to get them nice and crisp.
keywords: crispy, delicious, savory, appetizer, quick, easy, fast, vegan, vegetarian

title: Paprika Sweet Potato Sticks
description: The naturally sweet flavor of orange sweet potatoes meets a savory spice blend. A colorful, healthy, and unique side dish.
instructions: Peel the sweet potatoes and cut them into sticks about 0.6 inches thick.
In a large bowl, toss the potatoes with the oil until well coated.
Add salt, pepper, paprika, garlic powder, and onion powder, stirring vigorously to coat all the sticks with the spices.
Preheat the air fryer to 400°F.
Place the potatoes in the basket and cook for 11-15 minutes (depending on thickness).
Shake the basket halfway through cooking for even browning.
tip: Sweet potatoes tend to burn more easily than regular potatoes due to their sugar content: check them in the last 3 minutes of cooking.
keywords: fry, fried, crispy, tasty, vegetables, side dish, vegetarian, vegan, potatoes

title: Cajun Spiced French Fries
ingredients: A pinch of cayenne pepper (optional for extra heat)
description: Bring the flavors of Louisiana to your table with these vibrant fries. Air frying makes them light, while the Cajun blend adds an irresistible kick.
instructions: Cut the potatoes into even sticks and soak them in cold water for 15-20 minutes to remove excess starch.
Drain, rinse, and pat the potatoes very dry with a kitchen towel.
Preheat the air fryer to 385°F.
Toss the dried potatoes with the oil until evenly coated.
Cook in the preheated basket for 20-25 minutes, shaking the basket vigorously halfway through and at the three-quarter mark.
As soon as they are cooked and still hot, immediately sprinkle with the Cajun seasoning and toss well to coat.
tip: Always add the Cajun spices *after* cooking: if added before, they will tend to burn at 385°F and turn bitter.
keywords: frying, fried, crispy, tasty, vegetables, side dish, vegetarian, vegan, potatoes, spicy

title: Classic French Fries
ingredients: 2 large potatoes (yellow flesh or Russet ideal)
description: A timeless classic: golden, crispy homemade fries. The secret is soaking to remove starch and air-frying for maximum crunch with 80% less oil.
instructions: Cut the potatoes into sticks and soak them in a bowl of cold water for at least 20 minutes.
Drain the potatoes, rinse well, and dry them thoroughly (the drier they are, the crispier they get).
In a dry bowl, toss them with oil, garlic powder, and paprika, mixing well.
Preheat the air fryer to 383°F.
Cook for 25-28 minutes, shaking the basket every 10 minutes to ensure even cooking.
Salt only at the end, right after removing from the basket, and serve piping hot.
tip: Do not salt raw potatoes before cooking: salt draws out moisture and makes them soggy. Always salt at the end of the cooking process.
keywords: frying, fried, crispy, vegetables, side dish, vegetarian, vegan, potatoes

title: Crispy Crinkle Cut Fries
description: The crinkle shape holds sauces better and increases the surface area for extra crunch. Ready in just a few minutes straight from the freezer, without a single drop of added oil.
instructions: Pour the frozen fries directly into the air fryer basket.
Do not add any oil: the pre-fried industrial product already contains enough.
Set the temperature to 400°F and cook for 18-20 minutes.
Shake the basket two or three times during cooking to separate them and expose them all to the hot air evenly.
tip: If the basket is very full (more than 17.6 oz), you may need to add 3-4 minutes to the total cooking time.
keywords: frying, fried, crispy, tasty, potatoes, frozen, vegetables, side dish, vegetarian, vegan, fast, easy, quick

title: Southern-Style Buttermilk Fried Chicken
ingredients: 6.75 fl oz buttermilk (or milk with 1 tbsp lemon juice)
Salt and black pepper to taste
Generous amount of non-stick cooking spray
description: Southern US-style fried chicken: the buttermilk marinade makes it incredibly tender on the inside, while the spiced breading becomes super crispy thanks to air frying.
instructions: Submerge the chicken pieces in the buttermilk (in a bowl or sealed bag) and marinate in the fridge for at least 1.5 hours.
In a wide dish, mix the flour with the garlic, onion, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Remove the chicken from the marinade (without drying it too much) and coat it in the spiced flour, pressing well with your hands to ensure a thick breading.
Let the breaded pieces rest on a wire rack for 15 minutes: this is essential for the flour to hydrate so it doesn't fall off during cooking.
Preheat the air fryer to 383°F.
Arrange the chicken in the basket and spray it very generously with oil on all sides until no dry flour is visible.
Cook for 25 minutes, flipping the pieces halfway through and spraying more oil on any remaining white flour patches.
tip: Cooking spray is the secret: if you see white flour spots during cooking, spray them with oil to help them brown.
keywords: frying, fried, crispy, delicious, meat, main course, protein, chicken

title: Parmesan Zucchini Fries
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
description: A light and tasty snack: zucchini sticks coated in a flavorful cheesy breading. Crispy on the outside and tender on the inside, without deep frying.
instructions: Cut the zucchinis into sticks (remove the center part if it has too many seeds or excess water).
Prepare three shallow bowls: the first with flour, salt, and pepper; the second with beaten eggs and milk; the third with a mix of breadcrumbs and Parmesan.
Coat the sticks first in flour (shaking off the excess), then dip in the egg mixture, and finally press into the breadcrumb mix to coat thoroughly.
Preheat the air fryer to 375°F.
Arrange the zucchini sticks in a single layer in the air fryer basket and spray generously with cooking spray.
Cook for 10-12 minutes, turning them gently halfway through and spraying the other side with oil.
tip: For extra-crispy zucchini, use Panko (Japanese breadcrumbs) instead of regular breadcrumbs.
keywords: frying, fried, crispy, tasty, vegetables, side dish, vegetarian, appetizer, snack

title: Garlic Parmesan Chicken Wings
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
description: Flavorful chicken wings with a dry, tasty Parmesan and garlic coating. Perfect for a casual dinner or snacking in front of the TV.
instructions: Pat the chicken wings dry thoroughly with paper towels.
In a large bowl or plastic bag, mix the cornstarch, half of the Parmesan, garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
Add the wings to the mix and shake or toss to coat them evenly with the seasoned powder.
Preheat the air fryer to 383°F.
Arrange the wings in the basket, spray them with cooking spray, and cook for 25 minutes. Shake the basket or turn the wings with tongs halfway through.
Remove the hot wings and immediately sprinkle them with the remaining Parmesan so it melts slightly on the surface.
tip: Cornstarch is essential: it absorbs moisture from the chicken skin, turning it into a perfect crust.
keywords: meat, main course, high-protein, chicken, tasty, crispy, appetizer, frying, fried

title: Caribbean Jerk Chicken Wings
ingredients: 1 tsp dried thyme and 1/2 tsp rosemary
1 tsp garlic powder and 1 tsp onion powder
1 tsp paprika (or chili powder if you want them spicy)
Salt to taste and juice of 1 fresh lime
description: Intense, warm, and spicy flavors straight from Jamaica. The dry Jerk marinade gives the wings an unmistakable aromatic taste.
instructions: Pat the chicken wings dry with paper towels.
In a bowl, mix all the spice powders with the olive oil to create an aromatic paste.
Add the wings and toss with your hands to evenly coat every piece with the spiced seasoning.
Preheat the air fryer to 383°F.
Cook the wings in the basket for 25 minutes, remembering to flip them halfway through to prevent burning.
Remove the cooked wings and squeeze plenty of fresh lime juice over them before serving.
tip: If you love real heat, add half a finely minced Habanero chili to the marinade (be careful and wear gloves!).
keywords: meat, main course, protein, chicken, spicy, caribbean, tasty, entree

title: Ketchup and Mustard Glazed Wings
ingredients: 35 oz chicken wings (halved at the joints)
2 tbsp sweet soy sauce (or regular soy sauce + 1 tbsp honey)
description: A very simple marinade created with ingredients you already have in your pantry or fridge. The result is juicy, caramelized, and flavorful chicken.
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the ketchup, mustard, soy sauce, olive oil, and paprika.
Add the chicken wings to the sauce, cover with plastic wrap, and marinate in the fridge for at least 2 hours (up to 12 hours for an extra intense flavor).
Drain the wings from excess marinade (keep the marinade for later) and place them in the air fryer basket.
Cook at a gentler temperature, 340°F, for 18-20 minutes. Flip them halfway through.
For an extra glazed effect, brush the wings with the reserved marinade 3 minutes before they are done.
tip: Cook them at 340°F instead of the standard 385°F: sugary sauces (like ketchup and sweet soy) burn easily at higher temperatures.
keywords: meat, main course, protein, chicken, glazed, sweet-and-savory, delicious

title: Spicy Honey Sriracha Wings
ingredients: Garlic powder, onion powder, and paprika (1/2 teaspoon each)
3 tablespoons Sriracha sauce (adjust based on your heat tolerance)
1 tablespoon rice vinegar (or apple cider vinegar)
description: Extra crispy thanks to cornstarch, then coated in a glossy, irresistibly sweet and spicy Asian-style sauce.
instructions: Pat the wings dry and coat them in a bag with the cornstarch and powdered spices.
Preheat the air fryer to 383°F, place the wings inside, spray generously with cooking spray, and cook for 25-30 minutes, flipping halfway through.
While the chicken cooks, combine the honey, Sriracha, and vinegar in a small saucepan. Heat over low heat for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Remove the perfectly golden and crispy wings and toss them immediately into a large bowl.
Pour the warm sauce over the wings and toss vigorously to glaze every single one.
tip: Do not cook the wings already coated in the sauce: the honey will burn. Cook the chicken 'dry' and glaze it only at the end in a bowl.
keywords: meat, main course, protein, chicken, spicy, sweet and sour, asian, appetizer, delicious

title: Chicken Tikka Drumsticks
ingredients: 2.7 oz coconut milk (thick part) or Greek yogurt
1 small piece of fresh grated ginger and 1 garlic clove
description: Incredibly tender and aromatic chicken drumsticks, marinated in an enveloping blend of Indian spices and coconut milk. A flavor journey without leaving home.
instructions: Make two or three diagonal cuts on the meat of each drumstick: this will help the marinade penetrate deeply.
In a bowl, mix the coconut milk, tomato paste, all the spices, garlic, ginger, and salt.
Submerge the chicken, cover, and let marinate in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour.
Preheat the air fryer to 355°F. Remove the drumsticks from the marinade (leaving the excess clinging to the meat).
Cook in the basket for 20-25 minutes, flipping halfway through, until golden brown with nice tandoori-style char marks.
tip: Serve piping hot accompanied by steamed basmati rice and Naan bread to soak up the flavors.
keywords: meat, main course, protein, chicken, Indian, spiced, ethnic

title: Cajun Chicken Tenders
ingredients: 17.6 oz chicken breast or tenderloins cut into long strips
6.75 fl oz buttermilk (or milk with 1 tbsp lemon juice)
1 tsp garlic powder and 1 tsp onion powder
Salt to taste and non-stick cooking spray
description: Delicious chicken tenders marinated to stay juicy on the inside and breaded with zesty Cajun spices for a flavorful, crunchy crust.
instructions: Dip the chicken strips into the buttermilk mixed with hot sauce and let them rest in the fridge for at least one hour.

In a rectangular baking dish, mix the flour with Cajun spices, garlic, onion, and salt. Take a spoonful of the liquid marinade and drop it into the flour, mixing with your fingers: this will create small clumps that will become super crispy.
Drain the fillets and coat them well in the flour mixture, pressing down with your hands.
Preheat the air fryer to 383°F. Place the tenders in a single layer and spray them generously with cooking oil.
Cook for 12-14 minutes, flipping halfway through and spraying more oil on any spots where you still see dry flour.
tip: The clump trick: pouring a few drops of liquid marinade into the flour before breading creates those extra-crispy flakes typical of fast food.
keywords: frying, fried, crunchy, delicious, meat, main dish, protein, chicken, fast, easy, quick, spicy

title: Lemon and Garlic Chicken Drumsticks
ingredients: Juice and grated zest of 1 large organic lemon
Salt and black pepper to taste
description: The ultimate quick dinner: classic chicken drumsticks with extra crispy skin and a fresh aroma of lemon and Mediterranean herbs.
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the olive oil, lemon juice, lemon zest, garlic, paprika, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Pat the chicken dry with paper towels, place it in the bowl, and coat thoroughly. Let it marinate covered at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Preheat the air fryer to 383°F.
Place the drumsticks in the basket in a single layer, ensuring they do not overlap.
Cook for 20-25 minutes depending on size, flipping halfway through to ensure even browning.
tip: For extra crispy skin, thoroughly pat the chicken dry before placing it in the air fryer basket.
keywords: meat, main course, protein, chicken, mediterranean, easy, fast, quick

title: Mustard Glazed Chicken Thighs
description: The bold, pungent flavor of mustard pairs divinely with the smooth sweetness of maple in this incredibly easy and quick-to-prepare glaze.
instructions: In a small bowl, mix the mustard, maple syrup, and all the powdered spices together to create the glaze.
Pat the chicken thighs dry with paper towels, season with salt and pepper, and generously brush the glaze on all sides using a silicone brush (save a little for later).
Preheat the air fryer to 375°F.
Cook for 22-25 minutes. About 5-7 minutes before the end of cooking time, turn the chicken and brush it with the remaining glaze.
Serve piping hot once the glaze has become sticky and golden.
tip: Line the bottom of the basket (under the grill) with a piece of parchment paper or foil: the dripping mustard and sugar will tend to burn and make a mess of the base.
keywords: meat, main course, protein, chicken, sweet and sour, easy, fast, quick

title: Tender Yogurt and Rosemary Chicken Thighs
ingredients: 4 large chicken thighs or drumsticks (skin optional)
Salt and black pepper to taste
description: The yogurt marinade uses lactic acid to break down the chicken fibers, making it incredibly tender and juicy. A rustic, foolproof recipe.
instructions: In a large bowl, mix the Greek yogurt, olive oil, mustard, garlic, chopped rosemary needles, salt, and pepper.
Coat the chicken thoroughly with the mixture, ensuring it is well covered on all sides.
Cover with plastic wrap and let it marinate in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours (overnight is even better).
Remove the chicken, wiping off excess marinade, and preheat your air fryer to 385°F.
Place the chicken in the basket and cook for 30-35 minutes, turning halfway through. The yogurt will dry out to form a delicious, aromatic crust.
tip: If you love crispy skin, this recipe is not for you (the yogurt softens everything). It is ideal for boneless, skinless thighs, which will remain as tender as butter.
keywords: meat, main course, protein, chicken, mediterranean, tender

title: Extra Crispy Japanese Pork Katsu Cutlets
ingredients: 2 boneless pork chops or loin (approx. 6 oz each, 0.4 inches thick)
1/2 tsp garlic powder and 1/2 tsp onion powder
Salt and white pepper to taste
description: The famous Japanese Tonkatsu (pork cutlet) reimagined in a healthy way. Panko breadcrumbs ensure a thick, airy crust that is crispy yet incredibly light, cooked with just a light mist of oil spray.
instructions: Lightly score the edges of the fat on the pork chops with a knife to prevent curling during cooking. Flatten them with a meat mallet if they are thicker than 0.4-0.6 inches.
Prepare three wide bowls: flour; beaten eggs; Panko breadcrumbs mixed with spices, salt, and pepper.
Dredge the meat in the flour (shaking off any excess), then dip into the egg, and finally press firmly into the Panko to ensure maximum adhesion.
Generously spray both sides of the cutlets with oil and place them in the air fryer basket preheated to 365°F.
Cook for 14-16 minutes depending on thickness, flipping halfway through and spraying with a little more oil if you see any dry patches of Panko.
tip: For Katsu, regular breadcrumbs do NOT work: you must use Panko (available in most large supermarkets). It is what provides that signature large-flake, extra-crispy effect.
keywords: frying, fried, crispy, delicious, meat, main course, high protein, Japanese, ethnic, pork

title: Breaded Eggplant Medallions
ingredients: 1.8 oz grated Parmesan or Pecorino cheese
Olive oil spray or olive oil for brushing
description: Delicious eggplant slices wrapped in a savory, golden, cheesy crust. Perfect as an appetizer, a vegetarian treat, or as a component for a lighter eggplant parmigiana.
instructions: Wash the eggplant and remove the ends, then slice it into even rounds (about 0.4 inches thick).
Set up three shallow bowls: one with flour; one with beaten eggs, salt, and pepper; and one with breadcrumbs mixed with the grated cheese.
Dip the eggplant slices first in the flour, then coat thoroughly in the egg wash, and finally press them into the breadcrumb and cheese mixture.
Generously spray the breading with oil and place the slices in the air fryer basket in a single layer.
Cook at 400°F for about 10-12 minutes, flipping them halfway through to ensure they are crispy on both sides.
tip: For an extra-crunchy, schnitzel-style crust, dip the slices in the egg again after the breading and coat them a second time. The result is incredible.
keywords: frying, fried, crispy, tasty, vegetables, side dish, vegetarian, appetizer, snack

title: Homemade Golden Fish Sticks
ingredients: 14 oz thick white fish fillet (cod, plaice, hake)
1 tsp fish herb or spice mix (e.g., dried parsley, lemon zest)
description: A classic freezer staple, reimagined as a 100% wholesome, homemade version. Loved by kids and ready in just a few minutes.
instructions: Ensure the fish is boneless and pat it very dry with paper towels. Cut it into rectangular sticks about 1 inch thick.
Mix the flour with the spices, salt, and pepper in a shallow dish; beat the eggs in a second dish and place the breadcrumbs in a third.
Dip each stick first in the flour, shake off the excess, dip into the egg, and finally coat well with breadcrumbs, pressing gently.
Arrange the sticks in the air fryer basket in a single layer and spray the breading evenly with cooking spray.
Cook at 350°F for 8-10 minutes. Turn them very gently (using a spatula) halfway through to brown the bottom side as well.
tip: Fresh fish is delicate: do not use tongs when flipping halfway through or you risk breaking the sticks, use a silicone spatula to lift them from underneath.
keywords: frying, fried, crispy, delicious, fish, seafood, main course, sea, fast, easy, quick

title: Cereal-Crusted Chicken Bites
ingredients: 17.6 oz chicken breast, cut into large cubes
Salt, garlic powder, and onion powder to taste
description: The fast-food secret revealed: crushed corn flakes give these bites an incomparable and delicious crispy armor.
instructions: Vigorously beat the eggs in a bowl, mixing in the mustard and hot sauce (or paprika).
In another bowl, combine the flour with salt, garlic powder, and onion powder. On a large flat plate, coarsely crumble the corn flakes with your hands (do not pulverize them completely).
Dredge the chicken cubes in the flour, dip them into the spiced egg mixture, and then roll them in the corn flakes, pressing well to ensure they stick.
Place the bites in the air fryer basket, spacing them out, and spritz them with cooking spray.
Cook at 355°F for 15-18 minutes, flipping halfway through the cooking time.
tip: Place the corn flakes in a sealed freezer bag and roll over them with a rolling pin a few times: you will get the perfect crumbly consistency without making a mess in the kitchen.
keywords: frying, fried, crispy, delicious, meat, main course, protein, chicken, tasty

title: Sausage-Stuffed Mushroom Caps
ingredients: 8-10 medium-sized fresh and firm button or portobello mushrooms
1.8 oz shredded mild provolone or mozzarella cheese
description: A rustic, trattoria-style appetizer. The meaty mushrooms hold a savory sausage filling, and the air fryer ensures perfectly melted, golden cheese in just minutes.
instructions: Clean the mushrooms with a damp paper towel, gently remove the stems, and finely chop them. Set the caps aside.
In a small skillet, sauté the chopped stems with the crumbled sausage and the whole garlic clove (remove the garlic afterwards) for 5 minutes.
Transfer the lukewarm filling to a bowl and stir in the breadcrumbs, parsley, Parmesan, and most of the provolone.
Fill the mushroom caps with the mixture, forming a slight mound, and top with the remaining cheese.
Place the mushrooms in the air fryer basket and cook at a gentle heat (320°F) for 12-14 minutes, until the mushrooms are tender and the topping is golden and melted.
tip: Cooking at a lower temperature (320°F) is the secret: at 400°F, the mushrooms would dry out before they are cooked, and the cheese would burn in an instant.
keywords: meat, main course, protein, delicious, appetizer, happy hour, vegetables

title: Crispy Chicken Spring Rolls
ingredients: 12 rice paper sheets (or square phyllo dough sheets)
5.3 oz chicken breast, diced or ground
5.3 oz mixed vegetables (carrot, cabbage, leek), finely julienned
1.8 oz rice noodles or vermicelli, softened and chopped
description: All the flavor of the famous Asian appetizer in a light and crispy version. The air fryer eliminates the need for a pot of boiling oil, while still delivering a perfectly crunchy shell.
instructions: In a small wok or skillet, quickly stir-fry the chicken over high heat with a tablespoon of oil; once opaque, add the julienned vegetables and soy sauce, and cook for 5 minutes. Turn off the heat, add the vermicelli, and let the filling cool.
Quickly dip a sheet of rice paper in warm water to soften it, then place it on a clean kitchen towel.
Place two spoonfuls of filling in the center, fold the right and left edges toward the center, and roll up tightly like a cigar.
Brush the spring rolls very well with oil and place them in the air fryer basket, leaving space between each one.
Cook at 355°F for 15-18 minutes, turning them halfway through, until they are golden brown with crispy bubbles.
tip: If using rice paper, it is mandatory to thoroughly grease both the basket and the spring rolls, otherwise they will stick firmly and tear.
keywords: frying, fried, crispy, tasty, meat, high-protein, chicken, ethnic, Asian, vegetables, appetizer

title: Air Fryer Pigs in a Blanket
ingredients: 1 roll of pre-made rectangular puff pastry
12 cocktail sausages (small) or 4 large sausages cut into thirds
1 beaten egg or 2 tablespoons of milk for brushing
description: The legendary 'pigs in a blanket', the king of every snack buffet. In the air fryer, the pastry puffs up majestically, turning golden in half the time of a conventional oven.
instructions: Cut the puff pastry into strips about 1 inch wide.
Wrap each small sausage in a strip of puff pastry in a spiral or simply by rolling it up.
Seal the edges of the dough well by pinching them with wet fingers to prevent them from opening as they expand in the heat.
Brush the top of the pastry with the beaten egg (or milk) and, if desired, sprinkle with some sesame seeds.
Place them in the basket spaced apart and cook at 400°F for 10-12 minutes, until the pastry is puffed and golden brown.
tip: Always leave about an inch of space between each snack: puff pastry triples in volume during cooking and they risk sticking together in one big clump.
keywords: yeasted, savory, appetizer, fast, easy, quick, tasty

title: Juicy Roasted Chicken Breasts
ingredients: 2 whole chicken breasts (halved to create 4 portions of approximately 7 oz each)
1 tsp paprika or mixed dried herbs
Salt and black pepper to taste
description: Forget dry, rubbery chicken: the rapid hot air seals the outside of the meat instantly, cooking breasts that are tender, juicy, and never dry. Perfect for high-protein diets.
instructions: Pat the surface of the chicken dry with paper towels: removing moisture allows the spices to adhere and the oil to sizzle properly.
Toss the chicken with olive oil, salt, pepper, and your chosen spices.
Preheat the air fryer to 375°F.
Place the chicken breasts in the basket and cook for about 18-20 minutes (exact time depends on their thickness).
Crucial step: flip them halfway through cooking with tongs to sear both sides.
tip: To check if they are done without a meat thermometer, cut into the center: the inside should be opaque white, not translucent pink, while still appearing moist.
keywords: meat, main course, high-protein, chicken, fast, easy, quick, diet

title: BBQ Glazed Chicken Mix
ingredients: 1 tsp smoked paprika and 1 tsp garlic powder
Salt and black pepper to taste
description: An American-style steakhouse night! A mix of chicken marinated with a dry rub and then repeatedly glazed with sauce, which will caramelize thanks to the intense airflow.
instructions: Mix the brown sugar with paprika, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Pat the meat pieces dry and rub them vigorously so the spice mix sticks well to the skin. Let rest at room temperature for half an hour.
Place the chicken in the preheated air fryer basket and set to 383°F for 22-25 minutes.
With 8 minutes remaining (after about 15 minutes of cooking), open the basket and start brushing generous layers of BBQ sauce on all pieces.
Cook for 4 minutes, open, turn the pieces, and brush the opposite side. You will get a phenomenal sticky crust.
tip: Apply the sauce only at the end! If you air fry raw chicken already coated in BBQ sauce, the sugars in the sauce will carbonize in 10 minutes, making it bitter.
keywords: meat, main dish, protein, chicken, tasty, american

title: Sweet and Sour Honey Lemon Chicken Drumsticks
ingredients: Salt to taste and lemon wedges
description: The perfect balance between the zesty acidity of lemon and the warm notes of honey. The air frying process renders the skin fat, transforming it into a thin, glossy, and crispy glaze.
instructions: Create the marinade in a large mixing bowl by combining the honey, soy sauce, lemon juice, and garlic.
Toss the chicken drumsticks in the mixture and let them marinate, covered, in the refrigerator for about 1 hour.
Drain the meat well (do not discard the leftover marinade!) and arrange the drumsticks in the basket, slightly overlapping if necessary.
Cook at 375°F for 20-22 minutes. Drain any excess liquid marinade from the basket if too much accumulates.
During the last 5 minutes, use a silicone brush to apply the reserved marinade over the hot chicken to caramelize it.
tip: Honey gets very hot and can burn quickly; keep an eye on the drumsticks during the last 5 minutes, and if they darken too much, lower the temperature to 320°F.
keywords: meat, main course, protein, chicken, sweet and sour, citrus

title: Asian Five-Spice Chicken Thighs
ingredients: 3 tbsp Hoisin sauce (or thick sweet and sour sauce)
2 garlic cloves and 1 small piece of ginger, grated
2 tbsp honey and 2 tbsp dark soy sauce
description: For those nights when you want to travel with flavor: mahogany-colored chicken thighs, incredibly glazed and fragrant with the iconic spice blend of Cantonese cuisine.
instructions: Create a thick paste by combining the Hoisin, oyster sauce, garlic, ginger, five-spice powder, and one tablespoon each of honey and soy sauce.
Coat the chicken thighs with the mixture, ensuring it gets under the skin. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for 2 hours.
Remove the chicken and lightly wipe off excess marinade. Preheat the air fryer to 375°F.
Cook with the skin side down for the first 10 minutes, then flip them skin-side up for another 8-10 minutes.
Mix the remaining honey and soy sauce in a small bowl and brush onto the hot skin in the final minutes for a super-glossy effect.
tip: The Chinese five-spice blend contains cinnamon, star anise, and cloves: use it sparingly as the flavor is very potent and pervasive.
keywords: meat, main course, protein, chicken, asian, ethnic, chinese

title: Rustic Mediterranean Herb Roasted Chicken
ingredients: 8 assorted chicken pieces (e.g., 4 drumsticks and 4 thighs)
1 tablespoon Herbes de Provence mix, or dried thyme, rosemary, and oregano
description: The classic scent of a Sunday morning. An easy yet impressive dish: no fancy sauces, just excellent meat, a garlic-herb rub, and plenty of heat.
instructions: Pat the chicken pieces very dry.
Coat them with olive oil, using your hands to ensure an even, thin layer.
Sprinkle the garlic powder, dried herbs, salt (which will draw out moisture for a crispy skin), and pepper over both sides. Let rest outside the fridge for 30 minutes.
Place the pieces in the basket (bone-in meat needs to breathe, do not overlap) and set to 385°F.
Cook for 22-25 minutes, flipping halfway through to roast the base.
tip: Prefer garlic powder over fresh minced garlic, as fresh bits can easily burn and become bitter in the air fryer.
keywords: meat, main course, protein, chicken, roasted, easy, rustic

title: Sunday Whole Roasted Chicken
ingredients: 1 whole cleaned and gutted chicken (maximum 42-49 oz depending on your air fryer capacity)
3 tablespoons olive oil or melted butter
4 garlic cloves (to be inserted whole into the cavity) and 1 sprig of rosemary
1 teaspoon garlic powder and 1 teaspoon sweet paprika for the outside
Salt and plenty of black pepper
description: Cooking a whole chicken in an air fryer is not only possible, but it yields stellar results in half the time of a standard oven. The breast meat stays juicy, and the exterior gets crispy.
instructions: Check that the chicken fits in the basket before starting (if it touches the top heating element, it is too large and will burn).
Pat it dry thoroughly inside and out, then insert the 4 whole garlic cloves, the rosemary sprig, and half a lemon (if you have one) into the cavity. Tie the legs together with kitchen twine.
Coat the outer skin with oil or butter, salt, pepper, paprika, and garlic powder.
Place it in the basket, breast side down. Cook at 355°F for the first 30 minutes.
Using two spatulas or meat forks, flip the chicken (breast side up) and cook for another 20-25 minutes at 375°F to crisp up the skin.
tip: If you notice the breast skin is browning too quickly but the chicken is not yet cooked through, place a small piece of aluminum foil on top to act as a shield for the final minutes.
keywords: meat, main course, protein, chicken, roasted, sunday, family

title: Whole BBQ Glazed Chicken
description: A spectacular twist on the classic Sunday chicken: cooked first naked and then generously glazed at the end for a result reminiscent of authentic American street-style rotisserie.
instructions: Truss the legs and pat the skin dry. Rub the chicken with oil and season generously with salt and pepper all over.
Place it in the air fryer basket breast-side down, close, and cook at 355°F for 30 minutes.
After this time, flip the chicken breast-side up and let it roast for another 10 minutes.
The last 10 minutes are crucial: lower the temperature to 320°F and brush the exposed side with plenty of BBQ sauce.
Close for 5 minutes, open again, and add more sauce to build layers. Cook for the final 5 minutes or until perfectly glazed.
tip: Lower the temperature to 320°F when adding the BBQ sauce: this prevents the direct heat from instantly burning the sugar in the sauce, which would create smoke.
keywords: meat, main course, protein, chicken, american, delicious, roast

title: Homemade Parmesan Meatballs
ingredients: 14 oz ground meat (beef, or a pork/beef mix)
1.8 oz stale bread crumbs or bread
Fresh chopped parsley, salt, black pepper
description: The classic meatball, as tender as your grandmother's, but ready in the air fryer. You'll skip the grease and mess of pan-frying while achieving a wonderful result, perfect for adding to tomato sauce later.
instructions: Soak the bread in milk for a couple of minutes, squeeze it out, and place it in a large mixing bowl.
Add the meat, egg, Parmesan, spices, and parsley. Mix by hand until well combined and firm (do not overwork or they will become tough).
Shape into round meatballs about the size of a large walnut or a ping-pong ball.
Arrange them in the basket without overcrowding (the air needs to circulate) and lightly spray the tops with oil.
Cook at 385°F for 10-12 minutes, shaking the basket or turning them halfway through.
tip: If you love a golden-fried exterior, roll the raw meatballs in a small plate with a little breadcrumbs and spray them with oil before air frying.
keywords: meat, main course, high-protein, meatballs, easy, fast, quick, beef, pork

title: Cheesy Mexican Chicken Quesadillas
ingredients: 4 tortillas or thin flatbreads (corn/flour blend is best)
7 oz chicken breast, thinly sliced into strips
1 small bell pepper and half an onion, thinly sliced
5 oz melty cheese mix (Edam, Cheddar, Provolone)
1 heaping tablespoon Mexican Fajita seasoning (cumin, chili, garlic)
description: All the heat of Mexico in 15 minutes. First, air-fry the meat and vegetables like a fajita, then pack them into a tortilla stuffed with cheese for an extra crispy toast.
instructions: In a bowl, combine the chicken, bell pepper, onion, oil, and spices. Toss the mixture directly into the air fryer basket and cook at 375°F for 10 minutes, shaking halfway through.
Remove the cooked chicken and vegetables from the basket. Wipe the basket clean with a paper towel.
Distribute the cooked filling onto one half of each tortilla, top generously with shredded cheese, and fold the other half over to form a half-moon.
Place the quesadillas flat in the basket. Secure the top edge with a toothpick to prevent the fan from blowing the tortilla open.
Cook at 375°F for 4-5 minutes, until the bread is toasted and the cheese is melted and bubbling out of the sides.
tip: The toothpick is essential in the final step! Air fryer fans are very powerful and would lift the empty side of the tortilla, spilling the filling.
keywords: meat, main course, high-protein, chicken, ethnic, Mexican, fast, easy, quick, snack

title: Roasted Lamb on a Bed of Potatoes
ingredients: 35 oz lamb shoulder or leg (strictly boneless) or kid goat cut into large pieces
18 oz baby potatoes, washed and halved (or quartered if large)
Juice of half a lemon and plenty of dried oregano
A splash of vegetable broth or 4 oz warm water
description: Get the most out of your air fryer with a two-layer cooking method: the flavorful juices from the lamb will drip down, softening and seasoning the potatoes underneath. The perfect Sunday dish.
instructions: Mix the olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper. Rub this marinade vigorously onto the lamb and let it rest for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Place the potatoes in the bottom of your air fryer basket and season to taste. Pour the broth or water over them.
If your air fryer allows, place the separator rack over the potatoes and arrange the meat on top (alternatively, simply place the roast directly on top of the potatoes).
Cook at 355°F for about 45-50 minutes total.
At the 25-minute mark, temporarily remove the meat to a plate to toss the potatoes, which will begin to cook in the drippings. Flip the meat and return to the air fryer to finish cooking.
tip: Make sure to debone and butterly the roast: cuts that are too thick may hit the heating element and cook unevenly on the inside.
keywords: meat, main course, protein, lamb, roast, sunday, potatoes, vegetables, side dish

title: Tender Yogurt Marinated Chicken Skewers
ingredients: 14 oz of chicken breast or thighs cut into 1.2-inch cubes
3.5 oz of Greek yogurt (plain, whole milk)
1 garlic clove minced, salt and pepper to taste
1 teaspoon sweet paprika and 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
Wooden skewers (short sticks to fit in the air fryer basket)
description: A classic Middle Eastern technique that never fails: the thick yogurt marinade tenderizes the lean fibers of the chicken breast, creating deliciously fragrant and juicy skewers.
instructions: Mix the yogurt with oil, garlic, paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper to create a flavorful orange cream.
Add the chicken pieces and coat them thoroughly. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours (4 hours is ideal).
If using wooden skewers, soak them in cold water for 10 minutes to prevent them from charring under the heat.
Thread the chicken pieces onto the skewers, allowing excess marinade to drip off. Place them in the preheated air fryer basket.
Cook at 385°F for 12-14 minutes. To brown them evenly on all sides, open the basket and turn the skewers halfway through cooking.
tip: Make sure to measure your skewers to ensure they are shorter than the diagonal of your square air fryer basket!
keywords: meat, main course, high protein, chicken, skewers, ethnic, middle eastern, fast, easy

title: Stuffed Pizza Roll
ingredients: 9.9 oz ready-made pizza dough (fresh or roll-out)
Salt, oregano, and garlic powder to taste
description: A fantastic dough roll stuffed with gooey cheeses and savory deli meats, perfect for casual dinners. The air fryer ensures even browning and a crispy texture in every slice.
instructions: Let the dough rest at room temperature, then roll it out on a lightly floured surface.
Evenly arrange the ham, cheese slices, and peppers on one half of the surface.
Carefully roll up the dough and seal the edges well to prevent the melted filling from leaking.
Brush the surface with the egg beaten with milk, then sprinkle with spices and a pinch of salt.
Place the roll in the preheated basket at 350°F and cook for 20 minutes, turning it very carefully halfway through the process.
tip: Brush the surface with egg wash and make small slits to let steam escape. Remember to shake the basket or turn the food halfway through the cooking time.
keywords: meat, main course, protein, savory, baked goods, appetizer

title: Golden Pork Tenderloin Roast
ingredients: 0.7 fl oz olive oil for brushing
Coarse salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
description: A rustic yet elegant main course that is incredibly simple to prepare. Air frying quickly seals the juices inside the meat, keeping it tender while creating a phenomenal crust on the outside.
instructions: Pat the pork tenderloins completely dry using paper towels.
Brush the surface of the meat evenly with oil and season generously with salt and pepper to your liking.
Place the whole pieces directly into the preheated air fryer basket.
Cook at 375°F for about 25-30 minutes, depending on the exact size of the cuts.
Remember to turn the meat halfway through the cooking time to ensure a crispy sear on both sides.
tip: Use a meat thermometer to check internal doneness without cutting into the tenderloin. Remember to shake the basket or turn the food halfway through the cooking time.
keywords: meat, main course, protein, savory

title: Balsamic Vinegar Beef Steak
ingredients: 32 oz of beef steak (flank or skirt cut)
description: A rich, sweet, and tangy marinade that enhances the intense flavor of beef. In just a few minutes of high-temperature cooking, you will get a succulent, restaurant-quality steak.
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the olive oil, balsamic vinegar, and Dijon mustard until emulsified.
Place the steak in the marinade, cover tightly with plastic wrap, and let it rest in the refrigerator for about two hours.
Remove the meat from the fridge and let it reach room temperature before cooking.
Place the steak into the preheated air fryer basket and run the steak program for 7 minutes.
Once cooked, slice against the grain, season with salt and pepper, and garnish with fresh basil leaves.
tip: Remember to shake the basket or flip the food halfway through the cooking time. Slice the meat against the grain after cooking for maximum tenderness.
keywords: meat, main course, protein, savory, fast, easy, quick

title: Herb-Crusted Ribeye Steak
ingredients: Dried oregano, rosemary, and sage to taste
description: An intense spice blend coats this ribeye, creating a delicious aromatic crust (the famous dry rub). The rapid circulation of hot air cooks the meat perfectly while keeping it juicy.
instructions: Prepare an aromatic rub by mixing the garlic powder, onion powder, oregano, rosemary, sage, and a dash of cayenne pepper in a small bowl.
Brush the steak evenly with olive oil on both sides to help the spices adhere.
Coat the entire surface of the steak with the spice rub, pressing gently with the palms of your hands to ensure it sticks.
Place the meat into the air fryer basket preheated to 400°F.
Cook quickly at a high temperature to sear in the juices, then slice after a short resting period.
tip: Remember to shake the basket or flip the food halfway through the cooking time. Let the meat rest for 10 minutes after cooking to redistribute the juices.
keywords: meat, main course, protein, savory, quick, easy, fast

title: New York Strip Steak with Fresh Herb Sauce
ingredients: 2 New York strip steaks (approx. 32 oz total)
4.4 fl oz extra virgin olive oil
Juice of 2 lemons and 4 garlic cloves
description: The extraordinary tenderness of roasted strip steak pairs beautifully with the vibrant acidity of this raw fresh herb sauce. Ideal for a special, quick, and highly impressive dinner.
instructions: Prepare the herb sauce by blending together the basil, cilantro, parsley, anchovies, shallots, and peeled garlic; then gradually incorporate the olive oil and lemon juice.
Lightly grease the surface of the steaks with neutral oil and season them generously with salt and black pepper.
Place the meat in the hot basket preheated to 400°F.
Cook for 7-9 minutes, depending on your preferred level of doneness.
Let the meat rest for a few moments before slicing, then serve topped with the prepared green emulsion.
tip: Remember to shake the basket or flip the food halfway through the cooking time. Let the meat rest for 5 minutes after cooking before cutting.
keywords: meat, main course, protein, quick, easy, fast

title: Roasted Bone-in Pork Chops
ingredients: 20 ml (0.7 fl oz) olive oil for brushing
Freshly ground salt and black pepper to taste
description: A classic and always satisfying main course. Cooking bone-in chops in the air fryer ensures they remain moist, tender, and achieve a succulent golden-brown crust.
instructions: Pat the surface of the pork chops dry thoroughly with paper towels to remove excess moisture, ensuring a perfect crust.
Brush them evenly with a thin layer of olive oil on both sides.
Season with salt and pepper, lightly rubbing the meat to help the seasonings penetrate.
Place the meat in the air fryer basket without overlapping, setting the temperature to 375°F.
Cook the meat, making sure to flip it halfway through to achieve an even, crispy sear.
tip: Brush the meat with oil to promote the Maillard reaction and browning. Remember to shake the basket or turn the food halfway through the cooking time.
keywords: meat, main course, protein, fast, easy, quick

title: Sweet and Spicy Pork Chops
ingredients: 0.11 oz onion powder and 0.11 oz garlic powder
description: Bring the fabulous sweet and smoky notes typical of the American South to your table. The brown sugar caramelizes beautifully in the air fryer thanks to the dry heat, creating a delicious dish.
instructions: Combine and mix well in a bowl the brown sugar, paprika, mustard powder, garlic, onion, salt, and pepper.
Coat the boneless pork chops thoroughly with the vegetable oil.
Bread the meat by rolling it in the dry spice mixture, pressing with your fingers so it adheres evenly.
Place the slices in the very hot basket, preheated to 400°F.
Cook for 11 minutes, then remove the pork chops and let them rest for a couple of minutes before serving.
tip: Spread the spices well over the meat to create a flavorful crust. Remember to shake the basket or turn the food halfway through the cooking time.
keywords: meat, main course, protein-rich, sweet, dinner, quick, easy, fast

title: Cheeseburger Sliders
ingredients: 4 slices of melting cheese and 4 small soft slider buns
description: Delicious, eye-catching, and perfect to enjoy with friends during an appetizer. Air-frying the meat gives you a pub-style sear without the mess or strong cooking odors in your kitchen.
instructions: In a bowl, mix the ground meat with Worcestershire sauce, mustard, finely grated onion, egg, salt, and pepper.
Shape the mixture into small, equal-sized patties and let them firm up in the refrigerator for about an hour.
Brush the mini burgers with olive oil and place them neatly in the air fryer preheated to 400°F.
Cook them, flipping halfway through the process to ensure a perfect charred color.
In the last minute, add the slice of cheese to let it melt softly, then assemble the sliders and serve.
tip: Remember to shake the basket or flip the food halfway through the cooking time. Add the cheese to the burger in the last minute of cooking to let it melt.
keywords: meat, main course, protein, savory, fast, easy, quick

title: Citrus-Scented Lamb Chops
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper to taste
description: These delicate cuts of meat become an absolute masterpiece when marinated for a long time and cooked quickly. The concentrated heat makes them incredibly fragrant on the outside and melt-in-your-mouth tender on the inside.
instructions: Remove the thin zest of the lemon, carefully avoiding the bitter white pith, then crush the garlic in a mortar.
Combine the crushed garlic with the olive oil and fragrant zest to create the base of the marinade.
Submerge the lamb chops, tossing to coat them on all sides, and let them rest in a cool place for about four hours.
Place them well-spaced on the rack of the preheated air fryer at 400°F.
Cook at high temperature for 10 minutes, remembering to flip them halfway through the cooking time.
tip: Let the meat marinate for 4 hours to tenderize and flavor it deeply. Remember to shake the basket or flip the food halfway through the suggested cooking time.
keywords: meat, main course, protein-rich, fast, easy, quick

title: Ground Beef Stuffed Pastries
ingredients: 2 rolls of store-bought shortcrust or puff pastry
description: This delicious South American-style appetizer is perfect for those who love bold flavors. The pastry shell will puff up quickly and become extra crispy, revealing a moist and spiced center.
instructions: Finely chop the scallions and sauté them gently in a pan with the oil for about 3 minutes.
Add the ground beef, season with the paprika, cook for another 10 minutes, and let the filling cool down completely.
Unroll the pastry and cut out regular circles, placing a generous portion of the cooled mixture in the center of each.
Fold the discs into a half-moon shape to form the classic pastries, pressing and sealing the edges so they do not open.
Brush them with the egg yolk diluted with a splash of water and cook in two batches at 400°F for 10 minutes each.
tip: Brush the empanadas with egg yolk mixed with water before baking. Remember to shake the basket or flip the food halfway through the cooking time.
keywords: meat, main course, protein, savory, snack, appetizer

title: Pork Roast with Vegetable Side
ingredients: 2 tablespoons honey and 2 tablespoons red wine vinegar
1 large eggplant, 2 zucchinis, and 1 bell pepper, chopped
4 cherry tomatoes and 1 large red onion
description: A sensational, complete one-dish meal. The roast releases its aromatic juices over the delicious vegetables below, creating a perfectly balanced flavor profile using only your air fryer.
instructions: Create a sauce by vigorously whisking together part of the olive oil, vinegar, honey, minced garlic, salt, and pepper in a jar.
Drizzle the pork tenderloins with the prepared marinade and refrigerate, covered, for at least two hours.
In a bowl, cut all the vegetables into uniform pieces, toss them with the remaining oil and basil, and arrange them evenly in the basket.
Place the drained roast directly on top of the fresh vegetables.
Cook everything at 375°F for 35 minutes, temporarily removing the meat to stir the vegetables during the last 15 minutes.
tip: Marinate the meat for at least 2 hours before cooking it with the vegetables. Remember to shake the basket or turn the food halfway through the cooking time.
keywords: meat, main course, protein, vegetables, side dish

title: Classic Beef Patties
ingredients: 0.7 fl oz extra virgin olive oil
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
description: No messy pans or grease splatters around the house: cooking your burgers in the air fryer ensures a flawless golden-brown crust. They remain irresistibly moist and succulent with every bite.
instructions: Remove the meat from the refrigerator a few minutes before cooking to allow it to reach room temperature.
Generously season both sides of the patties with salt and fragrant black pepper.
Lightly brush the surface with olive oil to promote beautiful browning.
Place the burgers in the preheated air fryer at 375°F, taking care not to press down on them with spatulas or tongs.
Cook, flipping the meat halfway through the indicated time to ensure a stunning crust on both sides.
tip: Flip the burger halfway through cooking for even browning on both sides.
keywords: meat, main course, protein, quick, easy, fast

title: Rich Stuffed Burgers with Meat and Vegetables
ingredients: 2 large red tomatoes, sliced into rounds
Tender lettuce leaves, washed and dried
1 garlic clove and 0.7 fl oz soy sauce
description: The satisfying experience of a great pub classic, brought into your own kitchen. The high temperature perfectly sears the raw patties and toasts the bun halves until fragrant.
instructions: Start by seasoning the ground beef with finely minced garlic, soy sauce, a drizzle of oil, and salt.
Mix the ingredients by hand until combined, then shape into four thick, round patties.
Place them in the preheated air fryer basket and cook at 400°F until they develop a rich, deep color.
Remove the meat and keep it warm; use the residual heat to toast the halved buns for a couple of minutes until golden brown.
Garnish the toasted bun bases by layering fresh lettuce, tomato slices, and the hot burger patties, then serve immediately.
tip: Lightly toast the buns in the air fryer while the meat is resting.
keywords: meat, main course, protein, vegetables, side dish, leavened, savory, appetizer, quick, easy, fast

title: Turkey Patties with Crunchy Slaw
ingredients: 1.2 oz sweet Hoisin sauce and a splash of soy sauce
Thin raw cabbage, carrot, and scallion slaw
description: The ideal choice for those seeking light alternatives to red meat, enhanced by amazing exotic flavors. The tenderness of the turkey is elevated and made incredibly tasty by a perfect and quick air-frying sear.
instructions: Combine the ground white meat in a large bowl with the pungent ginger, garlic, and Asian sauces.
Fold in the breadcrumbs and work the mixture vigorously with your fingers until the wet ingredients are fully absorbed.
Divide the spiced mixture into compact, uniform discs.
Place them in the refrigerator to firm up so they do not lose their shape during cooking.
Cook at 400°F, flipping halfway through, then serve in a good bun accompanied by the vibrant cabbage slaw.
tip: Let the patties chill in the fridge before cooking to help them maintain their shape.
keywords: meat, main course, protein, vegetables, side dish, fast, easy, quick

title: Hot Dogs with Sausage and Melted Cheese
ingredients: 2 fl oz of ketchup and diced pickles
description: A triumph of savory ingredients that embraces one of the most beloved street foods in the world. The air fryer not only melts the cheese to perfection but also softens the bread, making it absolutely delicious.
instructions: Pre-boil the large sausages by immersing them in a small pot of boiling water for a few minutes to tenderize them.
Gently sauté the red onion rings in a small pan over high heat.
Slice the soft buns lengthwise and spread a generous layer of sweet ketchup.
Place the sausage inside, top with onions, pickles, and finish by layering the yellow cheese slices on top.
Place the assembled hot dogs in the preheated basket for a few minutes just to melt the cheese and warm the bread.
tip: Pre-cook the sausages in boiling water before assembling and air frying the buns.
keywords: meat, main dish, high-protein, leavened, savory, appetizer, fast, easy, quick

title: Pork Rolls Wrapped in Prosciutto
ingredients: 16 oz of pork tenderloin, divided and thinned
0.7 oz of sun-dried tomatoes and 1 tbsp of olive oil
description: Incredible stuffed preparations that boast elegance yet are made in a flash. The thin prosciutto shell cooks in the air fryer, becoming flavorful and super crispy when sliced.
instructions: Gently pound the pork tenderloin portions to expand and flatten the surface of the meat.
Overlap the prosciutto slices on a work surface and place the pounded pork tenderloin on top.
Create a central strip by layering the raw spinach leaves, shredded melting cheese, and sun-dried tomatoes.
Roll up the entire preparation tightly to form a compact cylinder, tying it with kitchen twine if necessary.
Brush with a tiny amount of oil and cook in the preheated basket at 400°F until the outer casing becomes very crispy.
tip: Use kitchen twine to keep the rolls tightly closed during cooking.
keywords: meat, main course, protein, quick, easy, fast

title: Bacon-Wrapped Stuffed Jalapeños
ingredients: 12 jalapeño peppers or firm green sweet peppers
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
description: A spicy and vibrant combination that never fails to impress. The cheese mixes with the pork to become creamy, while the sustained heat wonderfully crisps the bacon.
instructions: Halve the peppers and carefully scrape out all the inner white pith and spicy seeds.
In a large bowl, combine the raw ground pork with the finely shredded cheese, seasoning the mixture with salt and pepper.
Generously spread and fill the hollowed peppers with the creamy mixture.
Wrap each half tightly with the bacon strips (securing with a toothpick if necessary).
Place the peppers in the air fryer basket and cook until golden brown and the bacon is sizzling.
tip: Remove the seeds from the jalapeños well to reduce the heat. Remember to shake the basket or flip the food halfway through the cooking time.
keywords: meat, main dish, protein, vegetables, side dish, sweet, dessert, breakfast, snack

title: Ground Beef and Herb Skewers
ingredients: 0.7 oz ras el hanout spice blend
0.7 fl oz olive oil and 0.07 oz cumin
description: Indulge in the pungent and deep flavors typical of oriental street food markets without having to travel. Shaped onto skewers, they roast perfectly, taking on that characteristic grilled aroma.
instructions: Finely chop the shallots and sauté them quickly in a pan with the oil to remove the sharp bite and make them translucent.
Place the ground beef in a bowl, adding the softened onions, all the fresh coriander leaves, and the exotic spice blend.
Mix and knead the mixture thoroughly, adjusting the seasoning to achieve a homogeneous blend.
Take generous portions of the mixture and shape them into long logs, pressing them firmly around the skewers.
Place them in the hot air fryer basket, laying them flat on the bottom, and roast them, flipping halfway through to ensure even cooking.
tip: Serve the kofta with a fresh yogurt and mint sauce.
keywords: air fry, fried, crispy, delicious, meat, main course, protein, savory, fast, easy, quick

title: Mint Lamb Meatballs
ingredients: 0.1 oz fresh mint and 0.35 oz fresh parsley
0.1 oz cumin and 0.17 fl oz hot sauce
0.68 fl oz lemon juice and 0.5 fl oz olive oil
description: Small but bold and rich tasty bites, exquisitely refreshed by the aromatic notes of lemon and mint. At a very high temperature, they develop an extra crispy crust.
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the ground lamb, finely minced garlic, and shallots.
Add the chopped herbs, liquids (lemon juice, olive oil, and hot sauce), and the fragrant cumin powder.
Mix everything thoroughly with your hands so that the flavors infuse beautifully into the meat fibers.
Easily shape the mixture into small round balls and place them in the refrigerator to firm up for at least thirty minutes.
Brush the meat with a final touch of oil and place them in the air fryer for eleven quick minutes at high heat.
tip: Serve with a yogurt or tzatziki sauce to balance the spices.
keywords: fast, easy, quick

title: Soy and Miso Glazed Meatballs
ingredients: 1.7 fl oz soy sauce and 1.7 fl oz sweet mirin
description: An irresistible delicacy with a rich, evocative flavor of oriental umami. Inside the air fryer vortex, the glossy glaze caramelizes beautifully on these wonderful meatballs.
instructions: Carefully incorporate the ground beef with the fermented bean paste (miso), sesame oil, and finely chopped fresh mint.
Lightly oil your fingers and roll small portions into identical spheres, then place them in the refrigerator to firm up briefly.
Whisk the brown sugar, soy sauce, and mirin together to create a wonderful, savory, and syrupy glaze.
Arrange the chilled meatballs in the preheated air fryer basket and start the cooking process.
During cooking, baste the meatballs repeatedly (about every two minutes) with the glaze using a brush to ensure they become beautifully caramelized.
tip: Brush the meatballs with the glaze every 2 minutes during cooking. Remember to shake the basket or turn the food halfway through the cooking time.
keywords: meat, main course, high protein, savory, fast, easy, quick

title: Air-Fried Whole Sausages
description: A simple and lightning-fast method to get juicy, golden-brown sausages. Hot air circulation cooks the inside to perfection while crisping the casing without needing to prick them.
instructions: Remove the sausages from the refrigerator a few minutes before cooking.
Place them directly in the air fryer basket in a single layer, ensuring they don't overlap to allow for even airflow.
Cook at 400°F for 8-10 minutes, depending on the thickness of the sausages.
Halfway through cooking, open the basket and gently turn them with tongs to ensure they brown evenly on all sides.
tip: Do not prick the sausages before cooking; this ensures they retain all their delicious juices inside.
keywords: sausages, meat, main course, quick, easy, fast

title: Mustard Glazed Sausage Spiral
ingredients: 28 oz pork sausage (in one single piece)
description: A spectacular rolled sausage, glazed with a sweet and tangy mixture that caramelizes during cooking. Perfect for indoor grilling without the annoying smoke of a barbecue.
instructions: In a small bowl, combine the honey, both types of mustard, the fresh thyme leaves, and a pinch of salt and pepper.
Roll the long sausage into a tight spiral. Skewer it with two wooden sticks crossed in an 'X' shape to keep it in place.
Generously brush the entire surface of the meat with the prepared mustard glaze.

title: Gourmet Steak and Horseradish Sandwich

title: Air Fryer Scotch Eggs

title: Soft Coconut Macaroons

title: Golden Avocado Wedges

title: Crispy Blooming Onion

description: A breathtaking American fair-style fried treat. The 'blooming' onion, sliced and battered, becomes a formidable fried sculpture whose petals melt in your mouth with a perfect crunch.

title: British-Style Breaded Cod
